_comment: ALLOWLIST, not a denylist — fail-closed by design (see
docs/proposals/config-only-deploy/context.md and
platform/auth/infra/config-only-allowed-params.json for the
full rationale). A parameter not named here is unsafe-by-default:
config-deploy.sh refuses to proceed if a live .env change would touch it.
This service is ECS Fargate, not Lambda — 'no code rebuild' means no
Docker build/ECR push, not 'no CFN update'. A CFN parameter change to the
ECS TaskDefinition (env vars, CPU/memory) already makes ECS roll new
tasks automatically as part of the stack update — no separate cold-start
touch is needed the way server/whatsapp-adjacent Lambda services need one.
Deliberately NOT listed, and why:
EnvironmentName            — identity of the stack itself.
ContainerImageUri          — always a fresh, immutable tag only a real
deploy's docker build+push produces;
config-only mode never builds/pushes an
image, so this always carries forward the
live stack's current value.
SessionBucketName          — the PHYSICAL resource name of the S3
bucket this template creates — changing it
makes CloudFormation try to REPLACE the
bucket (data loss), not a config tweak.
VpcId/VpcCidr/PrivateSubnetIds
— network topology, auto-detected from the
account when left as a placeholder in
.env; never a same-stack config update.
HostedZoneId/DomainName    — flips whether Route53 dynamic-DNS resources
exist at all, not a tunable.
SpotCapacity               — flips the ECS capacity provider strategy
(Spot vs on-demand) — a real infrastructure
topology change, not a tunable, even
though no code changes.
AuthEncryptionKey          — technically just a CFN NoEcho parameter,
but changing it makes every currently-
connected WhatsApp session's encrypted
auth state undecryptable, forcing a
re-scan of the QR code for every tenant.
Blast radius too large for a fast path —
requires a deliberate full deploy.
